classification.difficultyReason: Rearrange the two equations and select the secant–tangent identity to obtain the matching Cartesian option.

content.prompt:
The curve given by $x=3\sec t+1$ and $y=2\tan t-1$ can be expressed in Cartesian form as:

A. $\dfrac{(y+1)^2}{4}-\dfrac{(x-1)^2}{9}=1$

B. $\dfrac{(x+1)^2}{3}-\dfrac{(y-1)^2}{2}=1$

C. $\dfrac{(x-1)^2}{3}+\dfrac{(y+1)^2}{2}=1$

D. $\dfrac{(x-1)^2}{9}-\dfrac{(y+1)^2}{4}=1$

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\sec t&=\frac{x-1}{3}\\\tan t&=\frac{y+1}{2}\end{aligned}$$
Using $\sec^2t-\tan^2t=1$:
$$\begin{aligned}\left(\frac{x-1}{3}\right)^2-\left(\frac{y+1}{2}\right)^2&=1\\\frac{(x-1)^2}{9}-\frac{(y+1)^2}{4}&=1\end{aligned}$$
Correct answer: D.
